 Kali Chaudas 2026: Date, Puja Vidhi, Rituals and Significance
 Kali Chaudas 2026 falls on November 7. Check the puja muhurat, midnight rituals, Chaturdashi Tithi and significance of worshipping Goddess Kali during Diwali.

 Kali Chaudas 2026 will be observed on Saturday, November 7, as part of the Diwali festivities. Also known as Bhut Chaturdashi, the festival is particularly significant in Gujarat and other parts of western India. Devotees observe the occasion by worshipping Goddess Kali and seeking protection from negative energies and evil forces.
 Kali Chaudas falls during the Krishna Paksha Chaturdashi of the Hindu month of Kartik. Unlike some other Diwali rituals, its date is determined by the presence of Chaturdashi Tithi during midnight, known as Maha Nishita. This makes it important to distinguish Kali Chaudas from Roop Chaudas and Narak Chaturdashi, which may be observed on a different day.

 Kali Chaudas 2026: Date and Puja Muhurat 
 According to the New Delhi Panchang, Kali Chaudas will be observed on Saturday, November 7, 2026. The puja is traditionally performed during the midnight period. Here are the important Kali Chaudas 2026 timings: 
 Festival Date and Time  
 Kali Chaudas Saturday, November 7, 2026 
 Kali Chaudas Puja Muhurat 11:39 PM on Nov 7 to 12:31 AM on Nov 8 
 Chaturdashi Tithi Begins 10:47 AM on Nov 7, 2026 
 Chaturdashi Tithi Ends 11:27 AM on Nov 8, 2026 
 Hanuman Puja Saturday, Nov 7, 2026 
All timings are based on the local time of New Delhi, India. The midnight puja muhurat extends into the early hours of November 8.
 What is Kali Chaudas? 
 Kali Chaudas is a Hindu festival observed on the Chaturdashi Tithi during the Diwali period. It is also called Bhut Chaturdashi and is particularly popular in Gujarat and other western Indian regions. The festival is associated with the worship of Goddess Kali, who represents the destruction of evil and the protection of devotees. In certain traditional practices, prayers are also offered to Veer Vetal.

 Kali Chaudas has a distinct ritual significance because its observance is linked to the midnight period. According to the Panchang tradition, the date is selected based on whether Chaturdashi prevails during Maha Nishita, the auspicious midnight period.

 Kali Chaudas 2026: Puja vidhi and rituals 
 Kali Chaudas is observed through prayers and traditional rituals dedicated to Goddess Kali. Some customs involve visiting cremation grounds at midnight to offer prayers to the goddess and Veer Vetal. These practices are followed in certain traditions and are not common to every household. The observance may include: 
 Midnight worship: Devotees perform Kali Chaudas puja during the prescribed Maha Nishita period.
 Prayers to Goddess Kali: Worshippers seek the goddess's blessings for protection from evil forces and negative energies.
 Worship of Veer Vetal: Some regional traditions include prayers to Veer Vetal as part of the midnight observance.
 Traditional offerings: Devotees make offerings according to their family and regional customs.
 Hanuman worship: Hanuman puja is also associated with the occasion in some traditions.
Rituals may vary across communities. Devotees generally follow the customs practised in their families and local temples.
 Significance of Kali Chaudas

 Remove Ad 
 Kali Chaudas is associated with the victory of good over evil and the removal of negative influences. Worshipping Goddess Kali on this occasion is believed to bring courage, protection and spiritual strength. The festival also reflects the importance of midnight worship in certain Hindu traditions. Its connection with Maha Nishita distinguishes it from other observances that fall during the Diwali period.
 For devotees, Kali Chaudas is a time to seek divine protection and pray for peace and well-being. The festival holds particular cultural and religious importance in Gujarat, where it continues to be observed with traditional rituals.
 Kali Chaudas vs Roop Chaudas and Narak Chaturdashi 
 Kali Chaudas is often confused with Roop Chaudas and Narak Chaturdashi because all three observances are associated with the Chaturdashi Tithi during Diwali. However, their dates may differ depending on the timing of the Tithi and the religious tradition being followed.
 Kali Chaudas is determined by the presence of Chaturdashi during Maha Nishita, or midnight. Roop Chaudas and Narak Chaturdashi follow different ritual considerations and may fall a day earlier or later. Devotees should therefore check the specific observance and local Panchang rather than assuming that all three festivals always fall on the same date.
 Kali Chaudas and Kali Puja: Are they the same? 
 Kali Chaudas should also not be confused with Kali Puja, which is widely observed in West Bengal and other eastern Indian regions. Kali Chaudas is linked to Chaturdashi Tithi and the midnight Maha Nishita period. Kali Puja, on the other hand, is generally performed on Amavasya, the new moon night, during the Diwali celebrations.
 Although both observances involve the worship of Goddess Kali, they have different dates and ritual traditions.
